dek: The 21 best hookah lounges in NYC, ranked by the smoke, from Avenue A to Steinway Street, the Boogie Down and Bay Ridge.

slides.label: How I used to roll
slides.text: Back in the day, hookah was how the night *ended*. A bar crawl with the crew, a few drinks at a *speakeasy*, then low lights, good music and a pipe on the table till closing. Times changed. Now the hookah is *the main event*.

slides.label: No. 21 to 19
slides.text: *21. Al Nar Hookah Lounge*: "The fire" in Arabic, almost to Nassau. *20. Lounge 43*: Where the 6 train ends. DJ plays everything. *19. Mocha Hookah*: Tiny, never closes. Chess and dominoes.

slides.label: No. 18 to 16
slides.text: *18. Zamaan Hookah Bar*: House blends, patio with a retractable roof. *17. Gota Lounge*: Loud room, big music. Bring a squad. *16. NYC Huqqah Haus*: 40-plus flavors, spacious and spotless.

slides.label: No. 15 to 13
slides.text: *15. MOON SKY Hookah Lounge*: Climb a floor. The cloud does the rest. *14. Rotana Lounge*: One bowl runs for hours. *13. Eastern Nights*: 9.4 on Atly, the top score on Steinway.

slides.label: No. 12 to 10
slides.text: *12. Hayati Lounge*: For people who take the coal seriously. *11. Legacy Hookah Lounge & Bistro*: Leads the city's hookah strip. *10. Sky Lounge NYC*: A session without trading in the blazer.

slides.label: No. 9 to 7
slides.text: *9. The Oasis*: Big room, big music, big clouds. *8. La Sultana*: Speakeasy calm. The coals stay right. *7. Layla Lounge*: Low volume, slow pulls.

slides.label: No. 6 to 4
slides.text: *6. Desert Rain Lounge*: Pineapple heads and ice pipes. *5. Cozy Cafe*: Same flavor Tuesday as Saturday. *4. Mira Mediterranean*: The city's most hyped hookah room.

slides.label: The top 3
slides.text: *3. Eastside Story*: Rich flavor, smooth draw, deep seats. *2. Horus Cafe*: Ruling Avenue B for over a decade. *1. Kazuza*: About 50 flavors. The Den's Friday night.

Gen Z traded shots for spritzes, and the lounge with the water pipe is cashing in. Here are the 21 best hookah lounges in NYC, ranked by the smoke: the bowl, the coals, the flavor menu and the cloud.

New York's hookah story starts on Steinway Street in Astoria, the strip Newsday was calling Little Egypt by 1998. In 2004 the New York Times counted about 20 hookah bars in the whole city, roughly half of them on one stretch of Steinway. Rules passed in 2017 made new lounges far harder to open, so a lot of these rooms are survivors.

Back in the day, hookah was how the night ended: a bar crawl with the crew, a few drinks at a speakeasy, then low lights, good music and a pipe on the table till closing. Times changed. Now the hookah is the main event.

The top three are all downtown: Kazuza on Avenue A, Horus Cafe on Avenue B and Eastside Story on E 10th St. Queens gets six spots, Brooklyn three and the Bronx three. Tobacco is 21+ in NYC, so pace the session.

Nightlife is changing how it makes money. Eventbrite logged a 92% jump in sober-curious events from 2023 to 2024, and IBISWorld estimates US hookah lounges grew about 18% a year from 2020 to 2025.

When the drink stops being the main event, something else becomes the product. For hookah lounges, that is the session itself: the bowl, the coals, the flavor menu and the room.

New York adds a moat. Rules passed in 2017 require existing lounges that earn most of their revenue from hookah to hold a city permit, and they made new lounges far harder to open. The rooms that survived now operate with limited new competition.
